sanskrit: antarbhūmigatān nāgāñ jitvā tau ca mahāsurau samudravāsinaḥ sarvān mlecchajātīn vijigyatuḥ
english: Those two great asuras then conquered the serpents dwelling within the earth, and vanquished all the barbarian peoples who dwelt by the ocean.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvāṃ mahīṃ jetum ārabdhāv ugraśāsanau sainikāṃś ca samāhūya sutīkṣṇāṃ vācam ūcatuḥ
english: Then, determined to conquer the whole earth, those two of terrible command assembled their soldiers and addressed them in sharp words.

sanskrit: rājarṣayo mahāyajñair havyakavyair dvijātayaḥ tejo balaṃ ca devānāṃ vardhayanti śriyaṃ tathā
english: "The royal sages through great sacrifices, and the twice-born through oblations to gods and ancestors, increase the might, strength, and prosperity of the gods.

sanskrit: teṣām evaṃ pravṛddhānāṃ sarveṣām asuradviṣām saṃbhūya sarvair asmābhiḥ kāryaḥ sarvātmanā vadhaḥ
english: Therefore all those enemies of the asuras, as they thus grow powerful, must be slain by us all together with every means at our disposal."

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvān samādiśya pūrvatīre mahodadheḥ krūrāṃ matiṃ samāsthāya jagmatuḥ sarvatomukham
english: Having thus commanded all their forces, and having resolved upon a cruel course, the two set out from the eastern shore of the great ocean, marching in every direction.

sanskrit: yajñair yajante ye ke cid yājayanti ca ye dvijāḥ tān sarvān prasabhaṃ dṛṣṭvā balinau jaghnatus tadā
english: Whoever performed sacrifices, and whatever twice-born priests officiated at sacrifices — the mighty pair, upon seeing them all, struck them down by force.

sanskrit: āśrameṣv agnihotrāṇi ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām gṛhītvā prakṣipanty apsu viśrabdhāḥ sainikās tayoḥ
english: In the hermitages, the sacred fires of the self-purified sages were seized by their soldiers acting without fear and hurled into the waters.

sanskrit: tapodhanaiś ca ye śāpāḥ kruddhair uktā mahātmabhiḥ nākrāmanti tayos te 'pi varadānena jṛmbhatoḥ
english: Even the curses pronounced in anger by great-souled sages rich in austerities could not take hold of the two, for they were protected by the boon they had received.

sanskrit: nākrāmanti yadā śāpā bāṇā muktāḥ śilāsv iva niyamāṃs tadā parityajya vyadravanta dvijātayaḥ
english: When curses fell off like arrows loosed against stone, the twice-born, abandoning their vows, fled in all directions.

sanskrit: pṛthivyāṃ ye tapaḥsiddhā dāntāḥ śamaparāyaṇāḥ tayor bhayād dudruvus te vainateyād ivoragāḥ
english: Those on earth who were perfected through austerity, self-restrained and devoted to tranquility, fled in fear of the two just as serpents flee from Garuḍa.

sanskrit: mathitair āśramair bhagnair vikīrṇakalaśasruvaiḥ śūnyam āsīj jagat sarvaṃ kāleneva hataṃ yathā
english: With hermitages churned up and shattered, with sacred vessels and ladles scattered about, the whole world became desolate, as if struck down by time itself.

sanskrit: rājarṣibhir adṛśyadbhir ṛṣibhiś ca mahāsurau ubhau viniścayaṃ kṛtvā vikurvāte vadhaiṣiṇau
english: With royal sages and sages nowhere to be seen, the two great asuras, resolved and bent upon slaughter, wreaked havoc freely.

sanskrit: prabhinnakaraṭau mattau bhūtvā kuñjararūpiṇau saṃlīnān api durgeṣu ninyatur yamasādanam
english: Taking the form of elephants in rut with ichor streaming from their temples, the two dragged those hiding even in inaccessible places to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: siṃhau bhūtvā punar vyāghrau punaś cāntarhitāv ubhau tais tair upāyais tau krūrāv ṛṣīn dṛṣṭvā nijaghnatuḥ
english: Becoming lions, then tigers, then vanishing altogether, the two cruel ones, upon sighting sages, slew them through these and various other means.

sanskrit: nivṛttayajñasvādhyāyā praṇaṣṭanṛpatidvijā utsannotsavayajñā ca babhūva vasudhā tadā
english: Sacrifices and Vedic recitation ceased; kings and brahmin priests disappeared; festivals and solemn rites fell into disuse — thus the earth became at that time.

sanskrit: hāhābhūtā bhayārtā ca nivṛttavipaṇāpaṇā nivṛttadevakāryā ca puṇyodvāhavivarjitā
english: Full of wailing, stricken with fear, with markets and shops closed, with rites to the gods discontinued, and bereft of auspicious marriage celebrations.

sanskrit: nivṛttakṛṣigorakṣā vidhvastanagarāśramā asthikaṅkālasaṃkīrṇā bhūr babhūvogradarśanā
english: Agriculture and cattle-tending ceased; cities and hermitages were demolished; the earth became scattered with bones and skeletons — a terrible sight to behold.

sanskrit: nivṛttapitṛkāryaṃ ca nirvaṣaṭkāramaṅgalam jagat pratibhayākāraṃ duṣprekṣyam abhavat tadā
english: The rites for the ancestors were abandoned, and the auspicious vaṣaṭ-call fell silent; the world took on a fearful appearance and became difficult to look upon.

sanskrit: candrādityau grahās tārā nakṣatrāṇi divaukasaḥ jagmur viṣādaṃ tat karma dṛṣṭvā sundopasundayoḥ
english: The moon and the sun, the planets, the stars, the constellations, and the dwellers of heaven all fell into despair upon witnessing the deeds of Sunda and Upasunda.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvā diśo daityau jitvā krūreṇa karmaṇā niḥsapatnau kurukṣetre niveśam abhicakratuḥ
english: Having thus conquered all the quarters through cruel deeds, the two asuras, now without rivals, established their encampment at Kurukṣetra.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca tato devarṣayaḥ sarve siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ jagmus tadā parām ārtiṃ dṛṣṭvā tat kadanaṃ mahat
english: Nārada said: Then all the divine seers and the perfected supreme sages fell into great distress upon witnessing that vast slaughter.

sanskrit: te 'bhijagmur jitakrodhā jitātmāno jitendriyāḥ pitāmahasya bhavanaṃ jagataḥ kṛpayā tadā
english: Those who had conquered anger, conquered the self, and conquered the senses then went, out of compassion for the world, to the dwelling of the Grandfather.

sanskrit: tato dadṛśur āsīnaṃ saha devaiḥ pitāmaham siddhair brahmarṣibhiś caiva samantāt parivāritam
english: There they beheld the Grandfather seated together with the gods, surrounded on all sides by perfected ones and brahmin sages.

sanskrit: tatra devo mahādevas tatrāgnir vāyunā saha candrādityau ca dharmaś ca parameṣṭhī tathā budhaḥ
english: There was the great god Mahādeva, there was Agni along with Vāyu, the Moon and the Sun, Dharma, Parameṣṭhī, and Budha as well.

sanskrit: vaikhānasā vālakhilyā vānaprasthā marīcipāḥ ajāś caivāvimūḍhāś ca tejogarbhās tapasvinaḥ ṛṣayaḥ sarva evaite pitāmaham upāsate
english: The Vaikhānasas, the Vālakhilyas, the forest-dwellers, those who live on rays of light, the unborn, the undeluded, the sages who carry fire within them, the ascetics — all these sages were attending upon the Grandfather.

sanskrit: tato 'bhigamya sahitāḥ sarva eva maharṣayaḥ sundopasundayoḥ karma sarvam eva śaśaṃsire
english: Then, approaching together, all the great sages reported in full everything that Sunda and Upasunda had done.

sanskrit: yathākṛtaṃ yathā caiva kṛtaṃ yena krameṇa ca nyavedayaṃs tataḥ sarvam akhilena pitāmahe
english: What had been done, and in what manner it had been done, and in what sequence — they reported all of this in its entirety to the Grandfather.

sanskrit: tato devagaṇāḥ sarve te caiva paramarṣayaḥ tam evārthaṃ puraskṛtya pitāmaham acodayan
english: Then all the hosts of gods and those supreme sages, placing that very matter before him, urged the Grandfather to act.

sanskrit: tataḥ pitāmahaḥ śrutvā sarveṣāṃ tad vacas tadā muhūrtam iva saṃcintya kartavyasya viniścayam
english: The Grandfather, having heard the words of all, reflected for a moment and determined what needed to be done.

sanskrit: tayor vadhaṃ samuddiśya viśvakarmāṇam āhvayat dṛṣṭvā ca viśvakarmāṇaṃ vyādideśa pitāmahaḥ sṛjyatāṃ prārthanīyeha pramadeti mahātapāḥ
english: With a view to their destruction, he summoned Viśvakarmā; and seeing Viśvakarmā before him, the Grandfather of great austerity commanded: "Let a woman be created here, one to be sought after."

sanskrit: pitāmahaṃ namaskṛtya tadvākyam abhinandya ca nirmame yoṣitaṃ divyāṃ cintayitvā prayatnataḥ
english: Viśvakarmā, having bowed to the Grandfather and praised his words, pondered carefully and then fashioned a divine woman with great effort.

sanskrit: triṣu lokeṣu yat kiṃ cid bhūtaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam samānayad darśanīyaṃ tat tad yatnāt tatas tataḥ
english: From whatever existed in all three worlds, whether moving or stationary, he gathered with great care each and every beautiful thing.

sanskrit: koṭiśaś cāpi ratnāni tasyā gātre nyaveśayat tāṃ ratnasaṃghātamayīm asṛjad devarūpiṇīm
english: He set into her body tens of millions of jewels and created her composed of an accumulation of gems — a woman divine in form.

sanskrit: sā prayatnena mahatā nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā triṣu lokeṣu nārīṇāṃ rūpeṇāpratimābhavat
english: She, fashioned with great effort by Viśvakarmā, became in beauty unrivaled among all women in the three worlds.

sanskrit: na tasyāḥ sūkṣmam apy asti yad gātre rūpasaṃpadā na yuktaṃ yatra vā dṛṣṭir na sajjati nirīkṣatām
english: There was not the smallest part of her body that was not endowed with the perfection of beauty, nor any place where the gaze of those who looked upon her did not become fixed.

sanskrit: sā vigrahavatīva śrīḥ kāntarūpā vapuṣmatī jahāra sarvabhūtānāṃ cakṣūṃṣi ca manāṃsi ca
english: She was as if Śrī herself had taken bodily form — lovely in appearance, glorious of figure — and she stole the eyes and minds of all beings.

sanskrit: tilaṃ tilaṃ samānīya ratnānāṃ yad vinirmitā tilottamety atas tasyā nāma cakre pitāmahaḥ
english: Because she was fashioned by gathering jewels particle by particle — sesame-seed by sesame-seed (tila by tila) — the Grandfather gave her the name Tilottamā.

sanskrit: pitāmaha uvāca gaccha sundopasundābhyām asurābhyāṃ tilottame prārthanīyena rūpeṇa kuru bhadre pralobhanam
english: The Grandfather said: "Go, Tilottamā, to the asuras Sunda and Upasunda; with your irresistible beauty, dear one, bring about their temptation."

sanskrit: tvatkṛte darśanād eva rūpasaṃpatkṛtena vai virodhaḥ syād yathā tābhyām anyonyena tathā kuru
english: "Bring it about that merely by seeing you and through the perfection of your beauty, discord arises between the two of them against each other — arrange things thus."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca sā tatheti pratijñāya namaskṛtya pitāmaham cakāra maṇḍalaṃ tatra vibudhānāṃ pradakṣiṇam
english: Nārada said: She, promising "so be it" and bowing to the Grandfather, performed a circumambulation of the assembled wise ones there.

sanskrit: prāṅmukho bhagavān āste dakṣiṇena maheśvaraḥ devāś caivottareṇāsan sarvatas tv ṛṣayo 'bhavan
english: The venerable one sat facing east, Maheśvara was to the south, the gods sat to the north, and the sages were on every side.

sanskrit: kurvantyā tu tayā tatra maṇḍalaṃ tat pradakṣiṇam indraḥ sthāṇuś ca bhagavān dhairyeṇa pratyavasthitau
english: As she performed that circumambulation there, Indra and the venerable Sthāṇu remained steadfast through fortitude.

sanskrit: draṣṭukāmasya cātyarthaṃ gatāyāḥ pārśvatas tadā anyad añcitapakṣmāntaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ niḥsṛtaṃ mukham
english: As she passed to his side, for Brahmā who was exceedingly desirous of seeing her, another face emerged — a southern face with curved lashes.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhataḥ parivartantyāḥ paścimaṃ niḥsṛtaṃ mukham gatāyāś cottaraṃ pārśvam uttaraṃ niḥsṛtaṃ mukham
english: As she moved behind him, a western face emerged; as she passed to the northern side, a northern face emerged.

sanskrit: mahendrasyāpi netrāṇāṃ pārśvataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'grataḥ raktāntānāṃ viśālānāṃ sahasraṃ sarvato 'bhavat
english: For the great Indra too, a thousand of those wide eyes with reddened corners spread on every side — to his flanks, his back, and his front.

sanskrit: evaṃ caturmukhaḥ sthāṇur mahādevo 'bhavat purā tathā sahasranetraś ca babhūva balasūdanaḥ
english: Thus Sthāṇu, the great god, became four-faced in ancient times; and thus the Slayer of Bala, Indra, came to have a thousand eyes.

sanskrit: tathā devanikāyānām ṛṣīṇāṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ mukhāny abhipravartante yena yāti tilottamā
english: Likewise, from all the hosts of gods and from the sages in every direction, faces turned whichever way Tilottamā went.

sanskrit: tasyā gātre nipatitā teṣāṃ dṛṣṭir mahātmanām sarveṣām eva bhūyiṣṭham ṛte devaṃ pitāmaham
english: The gaze of those great-souled ones fell upon her body — the gaze of all of them for the most part, excepting only the divine Grandfather.

sanskrit: gacchantyās tu tadā devāḥ sarve ca paramarṣayaḥ kṛtam ity eva tat kāryaṃ menire rūpasaṃpadā
english: As she departed then, all the gods and the supreme sages deemed the task accomplished by reason of her perfection of beauty.

sanskrit: tilottamāyāṃ tu tadā gatāyāṃ lokabhāvanaḥ sarvān visarjayām āsa devān ṛṣigaṇāṃś ca tān
english: When Tilottamā had departed, the sustainer of the worlds dismissed all the gods and those hosts of sages.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca jitvā tu pṛthivīṃ daityau niḥsapatnau gatavyathau kṛtvā trailokyam avyagraṃ kṛtakṛtyau babhūvatuḥ
english: Nārada said: Having conquered the earth, the two asuras, without rivals, free from anxiety, having rendered the three worlds undisturbed, felt their purpose accomplished.

sanskrit: devagandharvayakṣāṇāṃ nāgapārthivarakṣasām ādāya sarvaratnāni parāṃ tuṣṭim upāgatau
english: Having seized all the jewels of the gods, gandharvas, yakṣas, nāgas, kings, and rākṣasas, the two attained the highest satisfaction.

sanskrit: yadā na pratiṣeddhāras tayoḥ santīha ke cana nirudyogau tadā bhūtvā vijahrāte 'marāv iva
english: When there were none left anywhere to oppose them, the two became free of exertion and sported like immortals.

sanskrit: strībhir mālyaiś ca gandhaiś ca bhakṣair bhojyaiś ca puṣkalaiḥ pānaiś ca vividhair hṛdyaiḥ parāṃ prītim avāpatuḥ
english: With women, with garlands and fragrances, with abundant food and delicacies to eat, and with various delightful beverages, the two attained the highest pleasure.

sanskrit: antaḥpure vanodyāne parvatopavaneṣu ca yathepsiteṣu deśeṣu vijahrāte 'marāv iva
english: In the inner apartments, in forest gardens, in mountain groves and woodland retreats — in whatever places they desired — the two sported like immortals.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cid vindhyasya pṛṣṭhe samaśilātale puṣpitāgreṣu śāleṣu vihāram abhijagmatuḥ
english: Then one day the two came to sport on the flat stone surface of the Vindhya's crest, amid the sāla trees whose tops were in full bloom.

sanskrit: divyeṣu sarvakāmeṣu samānīteṣu tatra tau varāsaneṣu saṃhṛṣṭau saha strībhir niṣedatuḥ
english: With all divine desirable things brought there, the two sat down with great delight upon excellent seats, together with their women.

sanskrit: tato vāditranṛttābhyām upātiṣṭhanta tau striyaḥ gītaiś ca stutisaṃyuktaiḥ prītyartham upajagmire
english: Then women attended upon the two with instrumental music and dance, and came forward with songs mingled with praises to give them pleasure.

sanskrit: tatas tilottamā tatra vane puṣpāṇi cinvatī veṣam ākṣiptam ādhāya raktenaikena vāsasā
english: Then Tilottamā, gathering flowers in that forest, donned a provocative garment of a single red cloth.

sanskrit: nadītīreṣu jātān sā karṇikārān vicinvatī śanair jagāma taṃ deśaṃ yatrāstāṃ tau mahāsurau
english: She, slowly gathering the karṇikāra flowers that grew on the riverbanks, moved quietly toward the place where the two great asuras sat.

sanskrit: tau tu pītvā varaṃ pānaṃ madaraktāntalocanau dṛṣṭvaiva tāṃ varārohāṃ vyathitau saṃbabhūvatuḥ
english: The two, having drunk excellent wine with reddened and intoxicated eyes, were overcome with agitation the very moment they saw that woman of beautiful hips.

sanskrit: tāv utpatyāsanaṃ hitvā jagmatur yatra sā sthitā ubhau ca kāmasaṃmattāv ubhau prārthayataś ca tām
english: The two leapt up, abandoning their seats, and went to where she stood; both, maddened with desire, both besought her.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇe tāṃ kare subhrūṃ sundo jagrāha pāṇinā upasundo 'pi jagrāha vāme pāṇau tilottamām
english: Sunda seized the fair-browed one by her right hand; Upasunda too grasped Tilottamā by her left hand.

sanskrit: varapradānamattau tāv aurasena balena ca dhanaratnamadābhyāṃ ca surāpānamadena ca
english: Intoxicated by the boon they had been granted, and by their own bodily strength, and by their intoxication with wealth and jewels, and by the intoxication of wine —

sanskrit: sarvair etair madair mattāv anyonyaṃ bhrukuṭīkṛtau madakāmasamāviṣṭau parasparam athocatuḥ
english: Maddened by all these intoxications, frowning at each other, seized by the madness of desire, the two then spoke to one another.

sanskrit: mama bhāryā tava gurur iti sundo 'bhyabhāṣata mama bhāryā tava vadhūr upasundo 'bhyabhāṣata
english: "She is my wife; to you she is an elder" — thus Sunda addressed him. "She is my wife; to you she is a daughter-in-law" — thus Upasunda addressed him.

sanskrit: naiṣā tava mamaiṣeti tatra tau manyur āviśat tasyā hetor gade bhīme tāv ubhāv apy agṛhṇatām
english: "She is not yours, she is mine" — at this, fury entered the two; and on her account both of them seized their terrible iron clubs.

sanskrit: tau pragṛhya gade bhīme tasyāḥ kāmena mohitau ahaṃ pūrvam ahaṃ pūrvam ity anyonyaṃ nijaghnatuḥ
english: Grasping those terrible clubs and deluded by desire for her, shouting "I am first! I am first!" at each other, the two struck one another down.

sanskrit: tau gadābhihatau bhīmau petatur dharaṇītale rudhireṇāvaliptāṅgau dvāv ivārkau nabhaścyutau
english: The two terrible ones, struck down by the clubs, fell to the surface of the earth with their bodies smeared in blood — like two suns fallen from the sky.

sanskrit: tatas tā vidrutā nāryaḥ sa ca daityagaṇas tadā pātālam agamat sarvo viṣādabhayakampitaḥ
english: Then those women fled, and the entire host of asuras retreated to the underworld, every one of them trembling with despair and fear.

sanskrit: tataḥ pitāmahas tatra saha devair maharṣibhiḥ ājagāma viśuddhātmā pūjayiṣyaṃs tilottamām
english: Then the Grandfather of pure soul came there together with the gods and great sages, desiring to honor Tilottamā.

sanskrit: vareṇa chanditā sā tu brahmaṇā prītim eva ha varayām āsa tatraināṃ prītaḥ prāha pitāmahaḥ
english: She, invited by Brahmā to choose a boon, chose simply joy itself; and the pleased Grandfather then addressed her there.

sanskrit: ādityacaritāṃl lokān vicariṣyasi bhāmini tejasā ca sudṛṣṭāṃ tvāṃ na kariṣyati kaś cana
english: "You shall roam the worlds that the sun traverses, O radiant one; and because of your brilliance, no one will be able to look at you directly."

sanskrit: evaṃ tasyai varaṃ dattvā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ indre trailokyam ādhāya brahmalokaṃ gataḥ prabhuḥ
english: Having thus bestowed the boon upon her, the lord Grandfather of all the worlds entrusted the three worlds to Indra and departed to Brahmaloka.

sanskrit: evaṃ tau sahitau bhūtvā sarvārtheṣv ekaniścayau tilottamārthe saṃkruddhāv anyonyam abhijaghnatuḥ
english: Thus those two, who had been united and of one resolve in all matters, became enraged with each other over Tilottamā and slew one another.

sanskrit: tasmād bravīmi vaḥ snehāt sarvān bharatasattamān yathā vo nātra bhedaḥ syāt sarveṣāṃ draupadīkṛte tathā kuruta bhadraṃ vo mama cet priyam icchatha
english: "Therefore I tell you out of affection, O best of the Bhāratas all: arrange things so that no discord arises among you all on account of Draupadī. Do so, may it be well with you — if you wish what is dear to me."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktā mahātmāno nāradena maharṣiṇā samayaṃ cakrire rājaṃs te 'nyonyena samāgatāḥ samakṣaṃ tasya devarṣer nāradasyāmitaujasaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the great sage Nārada, those great-souled ones, O king, came together with one another and made a compact in the very presence of that divine seer Nārada of boundless might.

sanskrit: draupadyā naḥ sahāsīnam anyo 'nyaṃ yo 'bhidarśayet sa no dvādaśa varṣāṇi brahmacārī vane vaset
english: "Whoever among us finds another sitting with Draupadī shall live as a celibate student in the forest for twelve years on our behalf."

sanskrit: kṛte tu samaye tasmin pāṇḍavair dharmacāribhiḥ nārado 'py agamat prīta iṣṭaṃ deśaṃ mahāmuniḥ
english: When that compact had been made by the Pāṇḍavas who walked in righteousness, the great sage Nārada also departed, well pleased, to whatever abode he desired.

sanskrit: evaṃ taiḥ samayaḥ pūrvaṃ kṛto naradacoditaiḥ na cābhidyanta te sārve tadānyonyena bhārata
english: Thus was the compact previously made by them at Nārada's instigation; and all of them were never divided against one another from that time forth, O Bhārata.
